rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The coordinating waw may occur without a repeated conjunction, as in the phrase about the eighth and its dog.
rows.anchor: بل يجوز دخولها من غير تكرار قال تعالى ﴿ ويقولون سبعة وثامنهم كلبهم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the waw emphasizes the adjective’s firm attachment to its noun, signaling an established quality; such a clause may qualify an indefinite noun.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري دخلت الواو لتأكيد لصوق الصفة بالموصوف الدالة على إن اتصافه بها أمر ثابت مستقر

rows.speaker: جمال الدين بن مالك وأثير الدين
rows.claim: Ibn Malik and Athir al-Din say al-Zamakhshari was alone in proposing this emphatic use of waw.
rows.anchor: وقال الشيخ جمال الدين بن مالك في باب الاستثناء من شرح التسهيل وتابعه الشيخ أثير الدين إن الزمخشري تفرد بهذا القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects the claim that al-Zamakhshari was alone, since al-Azhari also recorded waw for emphasis.
rows.anchor: إن الزمخشري تفرد بهذا القول وليس كذلك فقد ذكر الأزهري في الأزهرية

rows.speaker: الأزهري
rows.claim: Al-Azhari gives emphatic waw after illa in ordinary Arabic and cites Qur'anic examples of the construction.
rows.anchor: ذكر الأزهري في الأزهرية فقال وتأتي الواو للتأكيد نحو ما رأيت رجلا إلا وعليه ثوب حسن

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abu al-Baqa allows waw before clauses adjectivally modifying a noun; the construction resembles a circumstantial clause, so waw is admissible.
rows.anchor: وأجازه أبو البقاء أيضا في الآية

rows.speaker: ابن فارس
rows.claim: Ibn Faris prefers treating waw in the command about striking and not breaking the oath as extra, over coordination or a prohibition analysis.
rows.anchor: قال ابن فارس ( 4 ) والأول أجود

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One analysis treats waw in the Yusuf passage as extra; another reads the phrase as We did that in order to teach him.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وكذلك مكنا ليوسف في الأرض ولنعلمه ﴾ 5 قيل الواو زائدة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative explains the Yusuf phrase as an omitted predicate: We did that so that We might teach him.
rows.anchor: وقيل ولنعلمه ( 6 ) فعلنا ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction with waw in protection from every devil can be parsed with an omitted verb: We did that as protection.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وحفظا من كل شيطان ﴾ 7 أي وحفظا فعلنا ذلك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A reported view treats the waw in the opening of Paradise's gates as emphatic and extra.
rows.anchor: وقيل في قوله ﴿ وفتحت أبوابها ﴾ 9 إنها زائدة للتأكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the waw is conjunctive; the answer to idha is omitted and means that the saved entered Paradise.
rows.anchor: والصحيح أنها عاطفة وجواب إذا محذوف أي سعدوا وأدخلوا

rows.speaker: بعض الصحابة
rows.claim: Some Companions hope the exception means the people of Paradise move to a higher station, such as divine pleasure or vision; the Prophet approved this hope.
rows.anchor: قول بعض 2 الصحابة وإنا لنرجو فوق ذلك مظهرا وصوبه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reads the first exception as people of Hell moving to extreme cold or another punishment, and the second as major sinners' rescue from punishment.
rows.anchor: وجعل الزمخشري الاستثناء الأول لخروج أهل النار إلى الزمهرير أو إلى نوع آخر من العذاب

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari argues by symmetry: since Paradise's exception cannot terminate bliss in light of the uncut gift, Hell's exception likewise cannot terminate punishment.
rows.anchor: وجعل الزمخشري الاستثناء الأول لخروج أهل النار إلى الزمهرير أو إلى نوع آخر من العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author keeps the first exception at its apparent sense, taking it as deliverance from Hell; there is no reason to abandon the ordinary force of exception.
rows.anchor: ظاهر الاستثناء هو الإخراج عن حكم ما قبله ولا موجب للعدول عن الظاهر في الاستثناء الأول فحمل على النجاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's doing what He wills explains both punishment and gracious rescue; the uncut gift clarifies that the second exception does not end Paradise's bliss.
rows.anchor: من العذاب والإنجاء منه بفضله ولا يتوجه عليه اعتراض أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects al-Zamakhshari's symmetry as strained: the second exception is not literal, so it does not require the first to depart from its apparent meaning.
rows.anchor: ورعاية هذا الباب أولى من رعاية الباب الذي توهم الزمخشري

words: فَلَوْلَا كَانَ مِنَ الْقُرُونِ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lawla used for reproach or regret normally precedes a past verb; exhortation and reproach concern actions, so it takes a verb.
rows.anchor: والتوبيخ والتنديم فتختص بالماضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With a past verb, lawla may reproach past failure or exhort future action by shifting the verb's reference forward.
rows.anchor: يجوز بقاء نفر على معناه في المضي فيكون لولا توبيخا ويجوز أن يراد به الاستقبال فيكون تحضيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lawla may be separated from its verb by temporal clauses and an intervening conditional sentence; the second lawla repeats the first.
rows.anchor: وقد تفصل من الفعل بإذ وإذا معمولين له وبجملة شرطية معترضة

rows.speaker: الهروي
rows.claim: Al-Harawi gives lawla a third use as a question meaning hal; most authorities omit this category.
rows.anchor: الثالث للاستفهام بمعنى هل نحو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author takes the first example as an offer or request, rather than the interrogative category.
rows.anchor: والظاهر إن الأولى للعرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author reads the second example like lawla in reproaches such as asking why witnesses were not brought.
rows.anchor: والظاهر إن الأولى للعرض والثانية مثل

words: فَلَوْلَا كَانَ مِنَ الْقُرُونِ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ
rows.speaker: ابن فارس والهروي
rows.claim: Ibn Faris and al-Harawi report a fourth use of lawla for negation, meaning lam, in the examples about a believing town and earlier generations.
rows.anchor: ذكره ابن فارس في كتاب فقه العربية والهروي في الأزهية

words: فَلَوْلَا كَانَ مِنَ الْقُرُونِ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers the apparent exhortative sense, supported by Ubayy's reading fahlā; reproach with a past verb nevertheless implies that the action did not occur.
rows.anchor: والظاهر إن المراد فهلا ويؤيده أنها في مصحف أبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hyperbole intensifies an established quality beyond what listeners usually find plausible or mentally possible.
rows.anchor: المبالغة وهي أن يكون للشيء صفة ثابتة فتزيد في التعريف بمقدار شدته أو ضعفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The layered darkness image amplifies darkness through the sea, a wave above it, and a cloud above the wave.
rows.anchor: ومن أحسنها قوله تعالى ﴿ أو كظلمات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hearts reaching throats means they nearly reached them, since a heart actually leaving its place would kill its owner.
rows.anchor: أي كادت تبلغ لأن القلب إذا زال عن موضعه مات صاحبه

rows.speaker: الفراء وغيره
rows.claim: Al-Farra and others allow a literal reading: fear swells the lungs, or continuous palpitations raise the heart toward the throat.
rows.anchor: لا يبعد أن ينهض بالقلب نحو الحنجرة ذكره الفراء وغيره

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari rejects supplying an implicit kādat, because kāda cannot be omitted.
rows.anchor: ورد ابن الانبارى 5 تقديرا كادت فإن كاد لا تضمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur'anic hyperbole also depicts plots moving mountains, the heavens nearly splitting, and sparks like castles or yellow camels.
rows.anchor: ومنه المبالغة في الوصف بطريق التشبيه كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text speaks hyperbolically of God's coming and of finding God, meaning the arrival of mighty signs and transfer to recompense.
rows.anchor: فجعل مجيء جلائل آياته مجيئا له سبحانه على المبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lightning almost snatching sight is nearer literal possibility because the verb yakādu shifts the expression from impossibility to possibility.
rows.anchor: ومنه ما جرى مجرى الحقيقة كقوله تعالى

words: سَوَاءٌ مِنْكُمْ مَنْ أَسَرَّ الْقَوْلَ وَمَنْ جَهَرَ بِهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse embeds hyperbole in a contrast: knowledge seems inaccessible to human addressees, but is not hyperbolic relative to God.
rows.anchor: فإن المبالغة في هذه الآية مدمجة في المقابلة

rows.speaker: الأقليشي
rows.claim: Al-Uqlishi distinguishes innate perfection in intellect, character, and conduct from excellence achieved through effort and removal of vices; one person has both only figuratively.
rows.anchor: قال الأقليشي 2 والحق أنك مهما نظرت إلى شخص

rows.speaker: ابن عبد السلام
rows.claim: Ibn Abd al-Salam asks why the more praiseworthy unseen is named before the witnessed, contrary to the usual rhetorical delay of the more praiseworthy.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عبد السلام في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن عبد السلام
rows.claim: Ibn Abd al-Salam answers that God has more witnessed objects of knowledge, so the witnessed deserves to be delayed.
rows.anchor: وأجاب بأن المشاهدات له أكثر من الغائب عنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author objects that God's unseen is innumerable; instead, the wording rises to the more praiseworthy to show the unseen and witnessed are equal in His knowledge.
rows.anchor: وقول الشيخ إن المشاهدات له أكثر فيه نظر بل في غيبه ما لايحصى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explicit equality between secret and public speech clarifies that unseen and witnessed are equal in God's knowledge.
rows.anchor: ويوضحه قوله تعالى ﴿ سواء منكم من أسر القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For multiple referents, unlike qualities of one referent, the better item comes first: horses, then mules, then donkeys.
rows.anchor: وأما الموصوفات فعلى العكس من ذلك فإنك تبدأ بالأفضل فتقول قام الأمير ونائبه وكاتبه

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: A cited poet illustrates the maxim that the more important matter is placed first, which appears to challenge delaying the more praiseworthy quality.
rows.anchor: وقال الشاعر … أبي دهرنا إسعافنا في نفوسنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The importance-first rule applies to distinct objects or purposes; delaying praise concerns two qualities of one thing, where reversing them would be pointless.
rows.anchor: المراد بقوله فقدم الأهم فالأهم فيما إذا كانا شيئين متغايرين

words: لَا بَيْعٌ فِيهِ وَلَا خُلَّةٌ وَلَا شَفَاعَةٌ
rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A sound report says the Prophet described moving Abu Talib from a deeper place in Hell to a shallow portion, despite the question of whether his uncle benefited.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث الصحيح أنهم قالوا يا رسول الله هل نفعت عمك أبا طالب فقال وجدته فنقلته إلى ضحضاح من النار

words: لَا بَيْعٌ فِيهِ وَلَا خُلَّةٌ وَلَا شَفَاعَةٌ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's repeated negations intensify its force: it denies worldly means of attaining aims and denies intercession itself, more strongly than merely denying its acceptance.
rows.anchor: وذكر ثالثا نفى الشفاعة أصلا وهى أبلغ من نفى قبولها فعاد الأمر إلى تكرار الجمل في الآيات ليفيد قوة الدلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same accusation appears with the definite phrase in al-Baqara and without the article in Al Imran, illustrating variation in definiteness.
rows.anchor: الرابع بالتعريف والتنكير كقوله فى البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Baqara has baladan as the second object and āminan its adjective; Ibrahim has al-balad as first object and āminan as second, pointing back to the barren valley.
rows.anchor: ﴿ بلدا ﴾ هنا هو المفعول الثانى و ﴿ آمنا ﴾ صفته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrases about victory vary in definiteness: one names God with the definite pair al-Aziz al-Hakim, the other uses indefinite adjectives.
rows.anchor: وقوله فى آل عمران ﴿ وما النصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Fussilat, the divine names receive emphatic definiteness and the pronoun huwa, reinforced by nearby wording; al-Araf keeps the unmarked form.
rows.anchor: لأنها فى حم مؤكدة بالتكرار بقوله ﴿ وما يلقاها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The adjective for plural nonhuman nouns is normally feminine singular, as in al-Baqara; Al Imran uses the alternative feminine plural form.
rows.anchor: لأن الأصل فى الجمع إذا كان واحد مذكر أن يقتصر فى الوصف على التأنيث

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Muslim report quotes the Prophet instructing readers to recite the two bright surahs, al-Baqara and Al Imran.
rows.anchor: كقوله اقرءوا الزهراوين البقرة وآل عمران رواه مسلم

rows.speaker: سعيد بن خالد
rows.claim: A report attributed to Sa'id b. Khalid says the Prophet recited the seven long surahs in one rakah and sometimes gathered the mufassal in one prayer; Ibn Abi Shayba transmits it.
rows.anchor: حديث سعيد بن خالد صلى رسول الله

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Al-Bukhari reports Ibn Masud naming Israil, al-Kahf, Maryam, Taha, and al-Anbiya as early treasured surahs, recited in their established sequence.
rows.anchor: وروى البخارى عن ابن مسعود رضى الله عنه قال فى بنى إسرائيل والكهف ومريم وطه والأنبياء إنهن من العتاق الأول

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Al-Bukhari reports that each night the Prophet joined his palms, breathed into them, and recited al-Ikhlas and the two protective surahs.
rows.anchor: وفى صحيح البخارى أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام كان إذا أوى إلى فراشه كل ليلة جمع كفيه ثم نفث فيهما فقرأ

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر النحاس
rows.claim: Al-Nahhas prefers that the Prophet set the surah order, citing a report from Ali and the Prophet's divisions of the Quran into the long surahs, hundreds, repeated pairs, and mufassal.
rows.anchor: المختار أن تأليف السور على هذا الترتيب من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وروى ذلك عن على بن أبى طالب

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر النحاس
rows.claim: Al-Nahhas says the ordering report shows the Quran was composed by the Prophet in that order before its later collection in one codex, and that al-Anfal is separate from Bara'a.
rows.anchor: وهذا الحديث يدل على أن تأليف القرآن مأخوذ عن النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم وأنه مؤلف من ذلك الوقت وإنما جمع فى المصحف

rows.speaker: ابن فارس
rows.claim: Ibn Faris distinguishes surah order, which the Companions arranged, from verse order and sequencing episodes, which the Prophet set as Gabriel conveyed God's instruction.
rows.anchor: جمع القرآن على ضربين أحدهما تأليف السور كتقديم السبع الطوال وتعقيبها بالمئين فهذا الضرب هو الذى تولاه الصحابة

rows.speaker: الكرماني
rows.claim: Al-Kirmani says the surah order is from God, preserved in the Guarded Tablet, and was the order reviewed with Gabriel annually and twice in the Prophet's final year.
rows.anchor: وكذا قال الكرمانى فى البرهان ترتيب السور هكذا هو عند الله وفى اللوح المحفوظ

rows.speaker: الصفار
rows.claim: Al-Saffar says the preceding usage is not established in Arab speech; for that meaning Arabs use madh or mundhu, ending at the time of reporting.
rows.anchor: قال الصفار وهذا الذي قاله غير محفوظ من كلامهم وإذا أرادت العرب هذا أنت فيه بمذ ومنذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Partitive min is indicated when it can be replaced by ba'd and the remainder still applies; Abraham settled some of his descendants in the valley.
rows.anchor: الثالث التبعيض ولها علامتان إن يقع موقعها وأن يعم ما قبلها ما بعدها إذا حذفت

rows.speaker: التراس
rows.claim: Al-Tarras is cited for saying min never separates from its explanatory-gender function; this use can be identified by substitution with alladhi and adjectival syntax.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنها لا تنفك عنه مطلقا حكاه التراس ولها علامتان إن يصح وضع الذي موضعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Explanatory min specifies which kind of ambiguous impurity is meant: idols; other impurities are excluded by separate evidence, and idols are part of impurity.
rows.anchor: وغيرها فلما اقتصر عليه لم يعلم المراد فلما صرح بذكر الأوثان علم أنها المراد من الجنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the promise to those among you who believe, min is explanatory rather than partitive because the address already refers to the believers themselves.
rows.anchor: أي الذين هم أنتم لأن الخطاب للمؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse combines three functions of min: origin in from the sky, partitive in some mountains, and explanatory for hail as a kind of mountain-like formation.
rows.anchor: وقد اجتمعت المعاني الثلاثة في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the verse about disbelievers, min first explains their categories, next is extra after a negative indefinite, and finally marks the source of good.
rows.anchor: فالأولى للبيان لأن الكافرين نوعان كتابيون ومشركون

rows.speaker: العسكري
rows.claim: Al-Askari distinguishes danan, used chiefly for entrusted or loaned things, from bakhl for owned qualities; knowledge resembles a loan, so the verse says danin.
rows.anchor: وفرق العسكري ( 4 ) بين البخل والضن بان الضن أصله إن يكون بالعواري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghibta and munafasa are praiseworthy: ghibta wishes for another's blessing without resenting it, while striving diligently for the same or better is munafasa.
rows.anchor: ومن ذلك الغبطة والمنافسة كلاهما محمود

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The prophetic saying that envy is allowed only in two cases means ghibta, wishing for a like blessing without grieving at the other's possession.
rows.anchor: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم لاحسد إلا في اثنتين واراد الغبطة وهي تمنى مثل ماله من غير إن يغتم لنيل غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When ghibta also prompts energetic effort toward an equal or better outcome, it becomes munafasa.
rows.anchor: فان انضم إلى ذلك الجد والتشمير إلى مثله أو خير منه فهو منافسة

rows.speaker: الغزالي
rows.claim: Al-Ghazali defines envy as wishing a blessing removed from someone entitled to it, sometimes with effort to remove it; on this definition, wishing its removal from an undeserving person is not envy.
rows.anchor: كذا ذكر الغزالي هذا القيد أعنى الاستحقاق وهو يقتضي أن تمنى زوالها عمن لايستحقها لا يكون حسدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sabil and tariq both mean path, but Quran uses sabil widely for good; tariq denotes good only when qualified or attached to a clarifying phrase.
rows.anchor: ومن ذلك السبيل والطريق وقد كثر استعمال السبيل في القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the past, ja'a and ata overlap, but ata is lighter; Quran favors yati/yatuna and uses the hamzated imperative form fa'ti/fa'tuna/fa'tu.
rows.anchor: ومن ذلك جاء وأتى يستويان في الماضي ويأتي أخف من يجيء وكذا في الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ja'a and dhahaba suit concrete entities, while ata and mada suit meanings or times; the verse says God took their light as though it were a tangible object.
rows.anchor: جاء يقال في الجواهر والأعيان وأتى في المعاني والأزمان وفي مقابلتها ذهب ومضى

words: إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنَا الذِّكْرَ وَإِنَّا لَهُ لَحَافِظُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ambiguous passages about God's essence, attributes, actions, and metaphorical wording are resolved by clear principles affirming God's incomparability and oneness.
rows.anchor: الأول الأشياء التي يجب ردها عند الإشكال إلى أصولها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For prophecy and the description of revelation, the decisive principles are that God preserves the Reminder and that the Prophet does not speak from desire.
rows.anchor: ومنه ضرب في تفصيل ذكر النبوة ووصف إلقاء الوحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When angelic and satanic promptings are difficult to distinguish, the clear standard is God's command to justice and beneficence; the following admonition calls people to remember.
rows.anchor: ومنه شيء يتقارب فيه بين اللمتين لمة الملك ولمة الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some passages admit many plausible interpretations, and the intended specific meaning cannot be decisively known to us.
rows.anchor: ومنه الآيات التي اختلف المفسرون فيها على أقوال كثيرة تحتملها الآية ولا يقطع على واحد من الأقوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mutashabih classification turns on whether the pause follows illa Allah and whether waw before those rooted in knowledge begins a new sentence or coordinates.
rows.anchor: الثاني أن هذه الآية من المتشابه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One group prefers a new sentence after illa Allah: only God knows the interpretation, while the learned affirm belief in what they do not know, like unintelligible ritual obligations.
rows.anchor: فمنهم من رجح أنها للاستئناف وأن الوقف على

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The separate-sentence reading favors taking the learned people's statement of belief as the predicate rather than a supplementary circumstantial clause.
rows.anchor: متردد بين كونه حالا فضلة وخبرا عمدة والثاني أولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Relative eloquence and verbal grace cannot be proved by formal logic; they are recognized through taste, like subtle differences in beauty.
rows.anchor: اعلم أن معرفة الفصيح والأفصح والرشيق والرشق والجلى والأجلى والعلى والأعلى من الكلام أمر لا يدرك إلا بالذوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not every grammarian, linguist, or jurist has literary taste; trained readers of rhetoric who practice prose, speeches, writing, and poetry judge the relative quality of speech.
rows.anchor: وليس كل من اشتغل بالنحو أو باللغة أو بالفقه

words: إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنَا الذِّكْرَ وَإِنَّا لَهُ لَحَافِظُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars agree that the Quran's wording and components must be mass-transmitted; the verified Sunni position also requires mass transmission of placement and order.
rows.anchor: النوع التاسع والثلاثون معرفة وجوب تواتره لاخلاف أن كل ما هو من القرآن يجب أن يكون متواترا فى أصله وأجزائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author argues that preservation and universal proclamation require mass transmission throughout the Quran's wording, location, and order; singularly transmitted material is not Quran.
rows.anchor: والحفظ إنما يتحقق بالتواتر

rows.speaker: كثير من الأصوليين
rows.claim: Many legal theorists require tawatur for Quranic wording alone, not placement or order; they point to al-Shafi'i's proof for the basmala at each surah's beginning.
rows.anchor: وذهب كثير من الأصوليين إلى أن التواتر شرط في ثبوت ما هو من القرآن بحسب أصله وليس بشرط فى محله ووضعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects the restricted view: without tawatur in placement, repeated Quranic refrains might not be transmitted reliably and non-Quranic material could be established.
rows.anchor: جاز سقوط كثير من القرآن المكرر وثبوت كثير مما ليس بقرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The uncreating referent may be idols, described with the rational relative man because Arabs treated them as objects of worship.
rows.anchor: والذي لايخلق المراد به الأصنام لأن الخطاب مع العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, man covers all beings worshiped besides God, rational and nonrational, using the rational form by predominance in a mixed group.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المراد ب من لا يخلق العموم الشامل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In an example listing crawling creatures, man applies to snakes and animals because rational and nonrational referents mix, so the rational form predominates.
rows.anchor: فعبر بها عمن يمشي على بطنه وهم الحيات وعمن يمشي على أربع وهم البهائم لاختلاطهم مع من يعقل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One explanation says ma is more common because nonrational things and their grammatical contexts are more numerous; man is reserved for the less common rational cases for stylistic fit.
rows.anchor: قيل إنما كان من لمن يعقل وما لما لا يعقل لأن مواضع ما في الكلام أكثر من مواضع من

rows.speaker: الإبياري
rows.claim: Al-Ibyari says the man/ma distinction applies to relative pronouns only, not conditionals, which require a verb and do not govern nouns.
rows.anchor: ذكر الإبياري في شرح البرهان إن اختصاص من بالعاقل وما بغيره مخصوص بالموصولتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative man can take a singular verb by form and a plural predicate by meaning, as in the wording about those who are Jews or Christians.
rows.anchor: فجعل اسم كان مفردا حملا على لفظ من وخبرها جمعا حملا على معناها

rows.speaker: ابن السراج وغيره
rows.claim: Ibn al-Sarraj and others disallow making both the subject and predicate follow man either by form or by meaning, though the Quran uses mixed agreement.
rows.anchor: وقالوا لا يجوز أن يحمل الاسم والخبر معا على اللفظ فيقال إلا من كان عاقلا أو يحملا معا على المعنى
